Terms of Use
Traffic Tickets Digital Service
This version in effect since 2025-03-13

The Traffic Tickets Digital Service (“TTDS”) provided by the Government of Alberta (“GoA”), provides secure access to online payment and resolution of traffic ticket(s), on the following terms and conditions (“Terms of Use”).
Users must agree to the terms of use before using TTDS.

User responsibilities
Users are responsible for ensuring that any information provided in the use of TTDS is complete, accurate, and up to date. Any false, inaccurate or misleading information will be considered a breach of the Terms of Use.

Governing law
These Terms of Use are governed by and interpreted in accordance with the laws in force in Alberta, and you agree and submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of courts in Alberta.

Additional terms
The GoA may set additional terms and conditions (“Additional Terms”) in relation to your use of TTDS by posting the additional terms on the TTDS website. It is the user's responsibility to review the additional terms.

Authorized purposes
You agree to use TTDS only for the purpose of resolving your traffic tickets with the GoA.

Remedies available to the GoA
If you breach any of these Terms of Use, the GoA, in its discretion, may take any steps that it determines necessary. These may include but are not limited to suspension or termination of your use of TTDS.

Use of TTDS
Use of TTDS is limited to person(s) who lawfully enter into and form contracts under the laws of Alberta. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, if you are under the age of 18, you must ensure that your parent of guardian reads and accepts these Terms of Use on your behalf prior to your use of the Service.

Use of representation
An accused may choose to be represented by an agent (e.g. friend, paid legal agent, etc.) or a lawyer. A reference to “Representative” in the Terms of Use and on TTDS includes agent or lawyers acting on behalf of the accused.
A representative acting for the accused must obtain the requisite consent before proceeding on their behalf including logging into TTDS and the use of the service.
A representative using TTDS on behalf of an accused must use their own email address to identify themselves as the representative. They must also indicate that they are a representative acting on behalf of the accused when submitting any type of service in TTDS. Failure to do so is a violation of the Terms of Use and the requested service will not be completed.
Where an agent is acting on behalf of the accused, it is mandatory for the agent to complete and upload a consent for representation form as a supporting document with the accused’s signature appended where necessary. This is a legal requirement for the proper disclosure of information to an agent. Failure to do so is a violation of the Terms of Use and the requested service will not be completed. Violations of this requirement may include but are not limited to suspension or termination of the agent’s use of TTDS.
If the representative wishes to withdraw their representation of the accused, they should notify the Advanced Projects and Traffic Office at JSG.TrafficTicketsSupport@gov.ab.ca prior to the court appearance date quoting the ticket number, name of the accused, and trial date where applicable. The representative should provide a client email address to be recorded on file in place of theirs whenever possible.
A representative whose representation has been withdrawn by the accused must not access TTDS or communicate with the Court on behalf of the accused.
Any communication purportedly made on behalf of the accused without the consent and prior knowledge of the accused is a violation of the Terms of Use. Any agent found to be acting for an accused without the required consent may be subject to consequences including suspension and termination of the agent’s use of TTDS up to and including such civil proceedings and criminal prosecution as may be warranted in the specific case.

No warranties
TTDS is provided ‘as is’ without warranty of any kind. The GoA does not warrant that TTDS will function without error, failure or interruption.

Limitation of liability
No action may be brought by any person against the GoA for any loss or damage of any kind caused by any reason or purpose including, without limitation, reliance on the functioning of TTDS.

Third party links
The TTDS may contain links to third party websites. The GoA provides these links for your benefit and convenience and does not take any responsibility for the content on the third party websites. A link to these websites does not imply an endorsement or recommendation of the products, services or information found there. A third party website or service may have a privacy policy different for that of the GoA, and may provide less security than the Service. The GoA disclaims all liability with regard to your access to linked websites. The GoA reserves the right to regularly review and re-evaluate any and all links and reserves the right to terminate any link without prior notification.

Communication
The GoA may send emails to you at the email address you provided about your use of TTDS, including, but not limited to, communications about payment, trial schedule, and online ticket disputes.

Abusive language
You must refrain from the use of abusive, threatening or inappropriate language in your communications with the GoA. Failure to comply may result in termination of your use of TTDS.

Transaction currency
All transactions within TTDS will be conducted in Canadian currency only.

Amendments
The GoA may amend these Terms of Use at any time without prior notice. Your acceptance of the Terms of Use constitutes your consent to the amended Terms of Use.

Contact Us
If you encounter technical issues with this platform, please contact JSG.TrafficTicketsSupport@gov.ab.ca.
